idea-plugin.name: OpenUnderstand Metrics
idea-plugin.description:
Java source metrics (Cyclomatic, CountLine, MaxNesting, CountDeclMethod, PercentLackOfCohesion, CountClassCoupled) from OpenUnderstand, an open-source implementation of the SciTools Understand API.

Requires python3 3.9+ on the path. The analyser ships with the plugin and installs itself into a virtualenv of its own the first time you press Analyse Project; nothing to configure.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.5.0
  • References agree with Understand at 0.9 or better everywhere. On thirteen Java projects, every reference kind, every entity kind and every project scores precision, recall and F1 of at least 0.9 against SciTools Understand. Before, 19 reference kinds were below that, among them calls (0.80 on the JSON benchmark, now 0.997).
  • Calls on inherited methods and fields, on statically imported members, and on elements of generic JDK containers (queue.peek().next()) now resolve, so the References view and the coupling and fan metrics see them.
  • Overloaded methods keep their own parameters and locals, so the Symbol Table lists one entry per declaration, as Understand does.
  • Metric macro F1 on the JSON benchmark 0.984 to 0.986, no metric below 0.9.
  • Ships analyser 0.6.0. The bundled virtualenv is keyed on the analyser version, so the first Analyse Project after updating builds a fresh one.
0.4.0
  • Java 9 to 25. Records, sealed types and permits, pattern matching for instanceof and switch, record patterns, switch expressions and yield, var, text blocks, local enums and interfaces, and module-info.java are parsed and analysed the way Understand analyses them. Before, a file using any of them failed to parse and showed no metrics at all.
  • On a Java 25 project (jenetics' incubator module) metric macro F1 against Understand went from 0.859 to 0.934, and no metric scores lower than before.
  • On Java 8 code nothing got worse and several metrics improved: on the JSON benchmark CountLineCode 0.964 to 0.994, CountDeclMethodPublic 0.955 to 0.982, and PercentLackOfCohesion 0.912 to 0.980.
  • Symbol Table and References buttons. The first lists every declared entity with its kind, type, parent and location; the second lists every reference to or from the selected entity, so selecting a row and pressing it again walks the graph.
  • Not supported: Java 25 compact source files (a method with no class around it).
  • Ships analyser 0.5.0. The bundled virtualenv is keyed on the analyser version, so the first Analyse Project after updating builds a fresh one.
0.3.0
  • Every metric in the tool window now agrees with SciTools Understand at F1 0.90 or better, measured over all 67 names on the JSON benchmark. The lowest was 0.500. Macro F1 is 0.970 and no metric fails to answer.
  • Largest movements: CountDeclClass 0.500 to 1.000, CountClassCoupled 0.585 to 0.906, CountOutput 0.655 to 0.916, CountInput 0.794 to 0.935, and CountClassBase and CountClassDerived to 1.000.
  • Anonymous classes and lambdas are entities of their own now, so they appear in the table with their own metrics instead of folding their contents into the enclosing method.
  • Ships analyser 0.4.0. The bundled virtualenv is keyed on the analyser version, so the first Analyse Project after updating builds a fresh one.
0.1.2
  • Fixed: the plugin icon was not well-formed XML. A double hyphen inside an XML comment ends the document for a strict parser, so the icon shipped in 0.1.1 failed to load.
  • Ships a newer build of the analyser.
0.1.1
  • Compatibility. Requires 2025.1 or later. 0.1.0 declared 2024.2+ but was built against 2025.1, and was binary incompatible with 2024.2 and 2024.3 -- it called a FileSaverDescriptor constructor that is a varargs one on those builds. Verified against 2025.1 through 2026.2.
  • Fixed: the analysis could fail with 'openunderstand' is not a package. The dumper was written to the shared temp directory, and Python puts a script's own directory first on its path, so a file left there by an earlier run shadowed the analyser. It is unpacked into a private directory now.
  • No interpreter to configure. The Python... button and the search of the machine are gone. The plugin builds a virtualenv of its own with python3 and installs the analyser it ships with, once, on the first Analyse Project.
  • Fixed: numeric columns sorted as text -- 10 came before 2 -- because the table reported every column as untyped. Double-clicking a row now only navigates, instead of also opening the cell for editing.
  • Metrics: CountDeclMethodProtected and CountDeclMethodDefault counted methods by matching the class name against the method's own name, so most classes reported 0. Both now agree with Understand (F1 1.000 and 0.949 on the JSON benchmark).
